title: Scope chain and lexical environment
learningObjectives: Explain scope chain and lexical environment and reason about JavaScript execution and function behaviour.

understand.concept: Lexical scope is determined by where code is written. When an identifier is not found in the current lexical environment, JavaScript searches outward through the enclosing environment chain. Closures retain access to the lexical environment in which a function was created.
understand.whyItMatters: Lexical scope makes variable access predictable and supports closures. Understanding it prevents accidental dependence on unrelated global variables.
understand.analogy: Scope lookup is like searching the current room, then the enclosing rooms, until the requested name is found.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scope, execution, identity, and scheduling follow language and engine semantics.

explain.narrative: The returned function still accesses topic from its enclosing function's lexical environment after createLesson has returned.
